title: Audit log aggregator TF module: multi-account CloudTrail sink + OpenSearch ILM + cold archive
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a reusable Terraform module that centralizes multi-account CloudTrail logs into a hardened S3 sink, ships events to an OpenSearch cluster with ILM policies, and applies lifecycle transitions to cold archive (Glacier/Archive) while preserving KMS encryption and auditability. This module must be deployable into customer VPCs for Redwood Private installs and support cloud-account delegation for cross-account trails.

Scope:
- TF module for: S3 sink + bucket policies + KMS key, cross-account CloudTrail configuration, optional CloudTrail Lake view, S3 event notification to log-shipper (Lambda or Fargate) or Kinesis Data Firehose, OpenSearch ingest pipeline and index templates, ILM policies and rollover, S3 lifecycle rule for cold archive, and healthcheck resources (synthetic canary writes + OpenSearch query job).
- Migration helpers for existing indices (zero-downtime ILM and template upgrades).
- Configurable retention tiers (hot-retain-days, warm-days, cold-days, archive-days) and an automated retention guardrail that prevents accidental retention reduction.

Out of scope: deep analytics dashboards or bespoke per-customer parser plugins. We will provide extensible hooks for customers to add processors.

Why this ticket: Current modules are fragmented across repos and copy-pasted per-customer. We need a single parametrized module to reduce drift, standardize audit controls, and enable safe upgrades.

Trade-offs / Decisions so far:
- Ship via Firehose when available to reduce custom lambda code; fall back to Lambda for older regions. Decision: provide both implementations behind a single boolean flag.
- Use index rollover with ILM (preferred) instead of time-based daily indices to improve write throughput. This increases complexity of migration but reduces cluster strain.
- Default retention conservative (90d hot) with explicit opt-in for shorter retention to satisfy regulated customers.

Security considerations: All S3 access enforced with bucket policies + KMS CMKs with key grants for cross-account CloudTrail principals. Module exposes option to integrate with customer KMS (kms_key_arn) or create a managed CMK. Security review required for key policy changes.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria array for flat checklist and automated tests that validate canary writes and ILM rollover.

Notes: includes links to design doc, PR template, and a runbook for index migration.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes tfvars to configure multi-account CloudTrail principals and validates principal ARNs
S3 sink created with enforce_ssl=true, block_public_access=true, versioning enabled, and KMS encryption applied
Firehose and Lambda shipping options both available and covered by unit tests
OpenSearch index template and ILM policy deployed and can perform a rollover without data loss
Automated canary: synth write to S3 and query OpenSearch within 60s; failures create alert to PagerDuty and CloudWatch alarm
Migration helper script allows reindex-from-template and index alias swap with <5m application-visible disruption (measured)
implementation_notes: Terraform design: split into submodules: bucket, kms, cloudtrail-config, shipper (firehose/lambda), opensearch-resources, monitoring. Keep single module entrypoint that composes submodules.
Provide acceptance testing via terratest and a lightweight AWS account sandbox. Tests: policy simulation, IAM assume role, canary write/read, ILM rollover simulation using tiny-size indices.

Index templates should include mappings for CloudTrail fields, ECS/CloudWatch logs, and generic JSON events. Include pipeline to add ingest timestamp, remove PII fields by default, and optional enrichment with account tags.

ILM policy default phases: hot (rollover at 30GB or 7d), warm (shrink/forcemerge), cold (freeze / move to search-optimized nodes), delete-to-archive: snapshot to S3 then lifecycle to Glacier for long-term retention.

We will implement snapshot->archive via automated snapshot repository to S3 followed by S3 lifecycle. This reduces OpenSearch storage while preserving searchable snapshots if customer enables the feature.

Support for cross-account CloudTrail: generate a CloudTrail role (assumable by member accounts) in the logging account and populate trust relationships. Include template for member-account CloudTrail configuration (documented example).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): deliver module alpha with S3+KMS+CloudTrail config and basic Firehose pipeline (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (integration): add OpenSearch templates, ILM, and canary + terratest suite (1.5 weeks)
Phase 3 (pilot): migrate one existing Private customer to new module with runbook and monitoring (1 week)
Phase 4 (GA): publish module to internal registry, update Private deployment playbooks and console docs (1 week)
Downgrade plan: keep previous module version available and provide terraform state migration scripts and a preview plan step to show index changes prior to apply
testing_plan: Unit: validate Terraform plan outputs (mocked), IAM policy ensures no wildcard '*' in statements
Integration: terratest in ephemeral AWS accounts that exercises cross-account CloudTrail, Firehose -> OpenSearch path
Chaos: simulate KMS key rotations and ensure rekeying process maintains access for trails and Firehose (document errors)
Performance: synthetic high-rtps load test to verify Firehose batching params and OpenSearch ingest throughput and backpressure behavior
E2E: canary agent writes a synthetic event to a 'canary' prefix in S3, a CloudWatch Event triggers shipper and event is found in OpenSearch index within SLAs
